shortcut_name: Tree structure makes the required subnetwork uniquely determined
evidence: "Remove non-critical leaves iteratively"; "Since m = n - 1 and the graph is connected with unique paths, it's a tree."
affordance_in_statement: The architecture of the station guarantees that the entire facility is fully contiguous, and that there is exactly one unique sequence of corridors connecting any pair of modules without retracing steps.
secondary_shortcut_name: Single critical module needs no corridors
removal_suggestion: There is no wording-only removal that preserves the task: the required answer is intrinsically the weighted Steiner subtree in a tree. A genuinely effective change would require replacing the tree setting with a general connected graph, which conflicts with the immutable m = n - 1 and connectivity requirements.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Prunes all non-critical leaves, leaving the unique minimal subtree containing the critical modules.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the architecture guarantees exactly one unique sequence of corridors connecting any pair of modules

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats the input as a tree and computes the forced subtree connecting all terminals.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the architecture guarantees exactly one unique sequence of corridors connecting any pair of modules

common_affordance: The input graph is a connected tree, so every path between critical modules is forced and the minimum connected subnetwork is simply the union of those paths.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: The implementation encountered a runtime failure, most plausibly from recursive traversal on a path-shaped tree of depth up to 200000; its tree assumption itself was appropriate.
The implementation produced a wrong answer, indicating that its pruning or subtree accounting failed to retain or sum exactly the edges in the minimal critical-module subtree.

recommended_edit: No valid single edit can defeat both surviving solutions while preserving this problem: the tree property is the core mathematical structure, not an incidental textual shortcut. To defeat them, change the task to a general connected graph and remove the forced-tree structure, which would require changing the immutable graph constraints.
regression_risk: Any superficial rewording of the tree guarantee will not defeat the survivors because m = n - 1 together with connectedness still forces a tree; it may also allow the already-defeated implementations to pass on their existing assumptions.
